common.tick_understood_in_the_box_to: Tick "Understood" in the box to be able to calibrate.
common.tap_again_the_machine_will_move: Tap again: the machine will move

advisor.run_a_ladder_in_the_test: Run a ladder in the Test section to know how much this axis really handles.
advisor.run_an_acceleration_ladder_in_the: Run an acceleration ladder in the Test section to know how far you can raise it without losing steps.
advisor.no_lost_steps_with_the_configured: No lost steps with the configured acceleration.
advisor.no_lost_steps_you_can_try: No lost steps. You can try higher if you want; leave ~20% margin for work.
advisor.pulses_aren_t_what_limits_the: Pulses aren't what limits the speed; the real limit is the motor (torque at high speed) and the mechanics.
advisor.you_re_close_to_the_board: You're close to the board's pulse limit. If you need more, lower the microstepping (x16 with interpolation is already smooth).
advisor.also_with_the_laser_the_areas: Also, with the laser the areas where it slows down burn more.
advisor.when_engraving_and_cutting_short_lines: When engraving and cutting short lines the axis almost never reaches max speed: raising ACCELERATION speeds jobs up more than raising speed.
advisor.enter_the_rated_current_below_general: Enter the rated current below (general, or that axis' or motor's own) to know if it's right (recommended: 50–85% of the rated current).
advisor.with_low_current_the_motor_loses: With low current the motor loses steps sooner. Raise it towards 70–85% of rated.
advisor.duet_recommends_50_85_of_rated: Duet recommends 50–85% of rated current. More heats motors and drivers without gaining much torque.
advisor.lower_the_max_speed_or_the: Lower the max speed or the microstepping of the fastest axis; with hiccups steps can be lost.
advisor.the_board_didn_t_generate_some: The board didn't generate some pulses on time (hiccups)
advisor.every_motor_without_its_own_data: every motor without its own data
advisor.steps_per_rev_tip: Full steps per motor revolution: 200 (1.8 degrees, the usual) or 400 (0.9 degrees). Used to calculate the RPM. Empty: uses the general one or 200.
advisor.estimate_of_how_much_of_the: Estimate of how much of the supply voltage the motor uses at that speed
advisor.pulses_per_second_of_each_motor: Pulses per second of each motor at max speed
advisor.distance_needed_to_reach_max_speed: Distance needed to reach max speed from standstill
advisor.table_note: "Now" are the limits in use: the ones the last M203 / M201 / M566 left (from config.g, the mode file or a macro). "Reaches speed in" = v² / (2·a): on lines shorter than twice that, the axis never reaches the maximum speed. "% ref." compares with the pulse ceiling of your board if you measured it in the Measure section; otherwise with the fixed table dc42 measured on a Duet 3 6HC (RRF 3.2, 1 motor). The Test section checks whether the motors lose steps.
advisor.motor_data_note: They are on the label or the datasheet of the motor. With this the recommended current is computed, and up to which speed the motor keeps its force with {v} V. Enter the general data and, if an axis (or one motor of an axis with several) is different, give it its own data.
advisor.current_too_high: {axis}: current too high, {ma} mA = {pct}% of rated ({a} A)
advisor.current_low: {axis}: low current, {ma} mA = {pct}% of rated ({a} A)
advisor.no_motor_data_for: No motor data to compare the current: {axes}
advisor.accel_distance: {axis}: with {a} mm/s² it takes {d} mm to reach {v} mm/s
advisor.pulse_rate_high: {axis}: at maximum speed it uses {pct}% of the reference pulse rate
advisor.pulse_rate_ok: {axis}: the board has plenty of pulse margin ({pct}% of the reference)
advisor.voltage_high: {axis}: at {v} mm/s the motor would need ~{pct}% of the {vin} V
advisor.voltage_high_text: Above ~{v} mm/s the motor starts losing force and may skip steps. Check with the Test before using that speed.
advisor.torque_ok: {axis}: the motor keeps its force up to ~{v} mm/s (estimated)
advisor.torque_ok_text: At the configured maximum speed it uses ~{pct}% of the available voltage.
advisor.lost_steps_speed: {axis}: lost steps in the test at {v} mm/min
advisor.your_max_already_there: your maximum ({v} mm/min) is already there or higher
advisor.highest_speed_passed: Highest speed that passed: {v}. Use ~80% of it as the working maximum.
advisor.speed_tested_ok: {axis}: speed tested OK up to {v} mm/min
advisor.your_accel_already_there: your acceleration ({a} mm/s²) is already there or higher
advisor.highest_accel_passed: Highest acceleration that passed: {a}. Use ~80% of it for working. With more acceleration the motor needs more torque right when starting and braking; if you want more, raise the current (within 50–85% of rated) or lower the maximum speed.
advisor.accel_tested_ok: {axis}: acceleration tested OK up to {a} mm/s²
advisor.accel_margin: Your configuration uses {a} mm/s²: you have room to raise it up to ~{max} mm/s² (80% of what was tested).
advisor.accel_not_tested: {axis}: acceleration not tested in this mode
advisor.intro: Compares the limits the machine uses now (and those of each mode file sys/mode*.g, if any) with the data of your motors and with the tests of the Test section. It changes nothing in the configuration: each piece of advice says which line to copy and into which file.
advisor.copy_failed: Could not copy: select it by hand
advisor.try_accel_ladder_first: Try an acceleration ladder in the Test section first.

crashFinal.it_stops_before_the_end_even: It stops before the end even with the least fine sensitivity. Check friction and the axis acceleration.
crashFinal.after_8_attempts_there_is_no: After 8 attempts there is no value that works. Check current, speed and mechanics.
crashFinal.no_margin_a_more_sensitive_value: No margin: a more sensitive value already gave false stalls. Test homing several times.
crashFinal.the_axis_is_too_short_for: The axis is too short for the test: lower the free stretch length.
crashFinal.the_duet_maestro_has_no_stallguard: The Duet Maestro has no StallGuard.
crashFinal.it_is_not_known_which_driver: It is not known which driver this board has: check its datasheet for StallGuard.
crashFinal.tmc2240_stallguard_only_works_in_stealth: TMC2240: StallGuard only works in stealthChop (M569 D3).
crashFinal.tmc2209_stallguard_only_works_in_stealth: TMC2209: StallGuard only works in stealthChop (M569 D3) and below the switch-over speed to spreadCycle (M569 V).
crashFinal.in_closed_loop_there_is_no: In closed loop there is no StallGuard: the motor must be in open loop (M569 D2).
crashFinal.external_drivers_6xd_1xd_boards_have: External drivers (6XD / 1XD boards) have no StallGuard: it cannot be used as an endstop.
crashFinal.carefully_hand_near_the_emergency_stop: carefully (hand near the emergency stop) to check it.
crashFinal.another_screen_is_saving_the_configurati: another screen is saving the configuration
crashFinal.config_g_changed_since_you_read: config.g changed since you read it. Tap "Show the change in config.g" again.
crashFinal.could_not_return_to_the_previous: Could not return to the previous sensitivity: restart the board to load the one in config.g.
crashFinal.could_not_read_the_previous_sensitivity: Could not read the previous sensitivity (M915): the test one stays until the board restarts and reloads config.g.
crashFinal.could_not_read_the_result_of: Could not read the result of the step.
crashFinal.check_the_values_past_the_limit: Check the values: past the limit 1-20 mm, free stretch 10 mm or more, H 20-2000.
crashFinal.saved_through_the_service_it_leaves: Saved through the service: it leaves a copy in the configuration history (WorkshopConfig > Backups).
crashFinal.saved_through_the_service_it_leaves_no_c: Saved through the service: it leaves a copy in the configuration history.
crashFinal.without_the_service_save_a_copy: Without the service save: a copy config.g.bak-(date) is made first.
crashFinal.config_g_already_has_these_lines: config.g already has these lines: nothing to change.
crashFinal.from_64_to_63_the_docs: From -64 to 63; the docs do not recommend below -10.
crashFinal.it_stopped_when_touching_the_end: It stopped when touching the end
crashFinal.nothing_is_saved_to_config_g: Nothing is saved to config.g until you see it and confirm it in step 4.
crashFinal.calibrating_the_machine_moves_on_its: CALIBRATING: THE MACHINE MOVES ON ITS OWN
crashFinal.each_motor_stops_on_its_own: Each motor stops on its own (squares the axis)
crashFinal.stops_all_motors_of_the_axis: Stops all motors of the axis when the first one stalls
crashFinal.one_reading_every_4_steps_fewer: One reading every 4 steps: fewer false stalls, detects a bit later
crashFinal.one_reading_per_full_step_detects: One reading per full step: detects sooner (the docs suggest it for homing)
crashFinal.go_past_the_limit_up_to: Go past the limit up to (mm)
crashFinal.2_how_it_moves_during_the: 2. How it moves during the test

crashFinal.coupled_kinematics: Kinematics {kin}: a move of {axis} moves more than one motor. The stall is detected by any of the drivers of the axis.

Less current = it detects with less force against the end (the docs suggest 30-50 %). Against the end it starts {approach} mm before the limit and goes up to {over} mm past it.

crashFinal.warn_3: and keep the nozzle, the laser or the cutter away from the material. No hands near the axis.

charts.speeds_in_mm_min_acceleration_in: Speeds in mm/min, acceleration in mm/s², jerk in mm/min. (i) = interpolated microsteps. The downloaded text also includes the full board replies.
charts.the_board_is_slow_to_answer: The board is slow to answer (more than 15 s).
charts.sg_empty: No StallGuard reading: the driver only measures it while the motor moves fast enough in spreadCycle (above the M569 V speed), never at standstill. Move the axis to see it.
charts.lower_more_load_on_the_motor: Lowest StallGuard between readings (M122): lower = more load; 0 = stalled motor. Only valid in spreadCycle and with speed.
charts.waiting_for_data_from_the_service: Waiting for data from the service...
charts.pick_one_or_several_they_use: Choose one or several. They use what the service already publishes (they ask nothing new of the board): with this page open, speed and pulses every second and the driver values every ~5 s. All show the same period up to now and the line is cut where there was no data. Keeps up to one hour while DWC is open.
charts.rep_max_speed: Maximum speed (M203): {v} mm/min · measured in the period: {m} mm/min
charts.rep_m915: M915: sensitivity S{s} · filter F{f} · from {h} full steps/s
charts.data_since_min: There is data from {n} min ago (since DWC was opened in this tab).
charts.report_intro: Reads from RepRapFirmware the configuration of every motor and driver (M350, M92, M906, M203, M201, M566, M569 and M915: read only, they change nothing) and joins it with the current state, the measured maximums and the alerts of the period chosen above ({period}).
charts.cruise_note: The one the planner gives the move being run, already with the limits (M203 / M201 / M566); not the instantaneous one.
charts.speed_note: The cruise speed of the move on the axes that move; on a diagonal each axis goes somewhat slower.
charts.current_note: Estimated from CS_ACTUAL at every reading of the drivers (~5 s); at rest it drops to the idle current.
charts.pulses_note: Sum of the steps per second of all its drivers (kHz).
charts.late_pulses_note: New delays of the step generator at each M122 reading: 0 is what is expected.
charts.vin_note: Motor supply (VIN): it drops to 0 with the power supply off.
charts.board_temperature_note: Of the microcontroller of the board; the driver does not measure degrees.
charts.no_alerts_in_period: No driver had a fault in the period.

enable.the_workshopservice_service_does_not_hav: The WorkshopService service does not have this function: update it.
enable.to_stop_it_enable_again_and: To stop it: Enable again and home. In case of danger, use the Emergency stop.
enable.while_released_do_not_use_the: While released, do not use the jog or other movement buttons: any movement enables them again by itself.
enable.a_vertical_axis_z_can_fall: A vertical axis (Z) can fall under its own weight: hold or support it first.
enable.the_released_motors_have_no_force: The released motors have NO FORCE: the head or gantry move by hand and the position (homing) is lost.
enable.a_live_job_is_being_sent: A live job is being sent: finish or close that job first.
enable.home_the_machine_before_working_again: Home the machine before working again.
enable.the_service_did_not_answer_within: The service did not answer within 15 s. Check the state before trying again.
enable.the_firmware_does_not_publish_it: the firmware does not publish it. The service reads it from every driver of the main board and remembers what was released through the API (also from another screen). On CAN boards (expansion) it cannot be read: the last request counts.
enable.motors_at_rest_are_not_disabled: motors at rest are not disabled, their current is reduced (M906 I, time with M906 T). Only with M906 I0 do they disable themselves.
enable.any_move_of_that_axis_jog: any move of that axis (jog, homing, a job) enables its motors again.
enable.m18_x_one_axis_m18_e0: M18 X (one axis), M18 E0 (one extruder), M18 (all). To enable, M17 with the same. Disabling an axis clears its homing. Enabling does not restore it.
enable.the_firmware_reprapfirmware_enables_and: the firmware (RepRapFirmware) enables and disables all motors of an axis together. If Z has two motors, disabling Z turns off both. There is no command to turn off just one.
enable.per_axis_or_extruder_not_per: Per axis or extruder, not per driver:
enable.what_can_and_cannot_be_done: What can and cannot be done
enable.there_are_no_axes_or_extruders: There are no axes or extruders with motors in the configuration.
enable.understood_i_will_release_the_motors: Understood: I will release the motors carefully
enable.releasing_motors_the_machine_is_without: Releasing motors: the machine is without that protection while it lasts
enable.disabling_a_motor_cuts_its_current: Releasing a motor cuts its current: it has no force and can be moved by hand. You can choose one, several or all.
enable.job_running_named_position_lost: A job is running ({name}): the position would be lost.
enable.job_running_position_lost: A job is running: the position would be lost.
enable.machine_busy_wait: The machine is busy ({state}): wait for it to finish.
enable.position_lost_axes_not_homed: The position is lost: {axes} will be left not homed. Home again before working.
enable.motor_without_force: The motor is left without force: it can be moved by hand.
enable.vertical_axis_can_fall: Vertical axis ({axes}): without force it can fall under its own weight. Hold or support what hangs before confirming.
enable.z_independent_motors: Z has {n} independent motors ({drivers}): without force they can get out of level. After homing, level again{g32}.
enable.kinematics_home_all: Kinematics {kin}: one motor moves more than one axis. Home all axes.
enable.extruder_released: The extruder is released: the filament can move.
enable.any_move_reenables: Any move of that motor (jog, homing, job) enables it again by itself.
enable.enable_no_position_axes: Enabling does not restore the position: {axes} still not homed.
enable.motor_may_jump: When it gets current the motor may jump slightly.
enable.idle_off_after_s: Idle (M906 I0): motors at rest disable themselves after {s} s and the axes lose their homing.
enable.idle_off: Idle (M906 I0): motors at rest disable themselves and the axes lose their homing.
enable.idle_reduce_after_s: Idle: motors at rest for more than {s} s drop to {pct} % of their current (M906 I). They stay enabled and keep their position.
enable.idle_reduce: Idle: motors at rest drop to {pct} % of their current (M906 I). They stay enabled and keep their position.
enable.power_off_nothing_to_do: The motor power supply is off: no motor has force. Releasing or enabling does nothing (and releasing would remove the homing).
enable.role_cannot_release: Your role can enable motors but not release them: releasing is for a technician or the administrator.

measure.the_service_did_not_read_m122: the service did not read M122 in time
measure.up_to_10_is_normal_clamp: Up to ±10 % is normal (clamp, temperature). Much less: the driver can't reach it (voltage, cable) or M906 isn't what you think. Much more: check M906 and the driver type.
measure.open_a_motor_wire_with_the: open a motor wire with the machine powered (for a multimeter in series): it can burn the driver.
measure.with_the_motor_still_each_coil: . With the motor still each coil carries a DC current that depends on the position; measuring both coils (A and B), the peak current is √(A² + B²) at any position.
measure.value_m906_not_a_measurement_the: value (M906), not a measurement: the drivers have no ammeter. To check it you need a
measure.what_the_page_shows_is_the: What the page shows is the
measure.real_current_of_each_motor_with: Real current of each motor (with a clamp meter)
measure.tap_again_back_to_dc42: Tap again: your measurement is deleted
measure.tap_again_energize: Tap again: motors at 100 % at rest (they get hot)
measure.idle_left_at_100: A clamp measurement was not finished: the motors are still at 100 % current at rest and get hot. Restore the reduction to {pct} %.
measure.it_s_used_as_the_reference: It's used as the reference in the Advisor and in Details instead of dc42's table.
measure.pulses_it_didn_t_generate_in: (pulses it didn't generate in time, M122). The first step with hiccups went over the ceiling. At the end the microstepping is restored; home afterwards.
measure.ceiling_intro: dc42's reference is a fixed table (Duet 3 6HC, RRF 3.2). This measures the one of your board and your firmware: it raises the microstepping of the axis to 1/{micro} (the board has to generate many more pulses per mm) and moves the axis at normal speeds, each time with more pulses per second. After each step it checks whether the firmware counted
measure.previous_measurement_interrupted: A previous measurement was interrupted: axis {axis} may have been left with the test microstepping.
measure.khz_per_motor_n_steps: kHz per motor. {n} possible step(s) with this axis
measure.steps_over_max_speed: (from {khz} kHz it would have to go faster than its maximum speed: they are not tested)
measure.axis_has_n_motors: Axis {axis} has {n} motors: the board generates {n} times those pulses.
measure.clamp_hint: With the clamp on one wire of each coil, √(A² + B²) should give ~{ma} mA.
measure.measured_peak_rms: Measured: {peak} mA peak = {rms} mA RMS ({dev} % of the configured value)
measure.step_n_of_total: Step {n} of {total}: {khz} kHz per motor ({v} mm/min at 1/{micro})
measure.ceiling_found: Ceiling: no hiccups up to {ok} kHz per motor; at {bad} kHz the firmware counted {n} hiccup(s). Saved as the reference. Home {axis} before working.
measure.ceiling_not_reached: No hiccups up to {ok} kHz (the highest that could be tested with the maximum speed of {axis}). The real ceiling is higher; {ok} kHz was saved as the minimum reference. Home {axis}.
measure.hiccups_first_step: Already in the first step ({khz} kHz) there were hiccups: start from fewer kHz.
measure.measurement_interrupted_error: The measurement was interrupted: {error}. If it stopped halfway, tap Restore and home.

axesTest.check_the_advisor_to_see_the: Check the Advisor to see the line to change. Since steps were lost, home before working.
axesTest.has_no_endstop_or_probe_to: has no endstop or probe to measure with
axesTest.no_tests_yet_they_re_saved: No tests yet (they're saved in sys/workshop/data/axis-test.csv).
axesTest.clear_the_work_area_and_keep: Clear the work area and keep your hand near the emergency stop. To stop NOW, use the Emergency Stop at the top.
axesTest.stops_by_itself_at_the_first: Stops by itself at the first one that loses steps.
axesTest.how_it_works_z_with_the: How it works (Z, with the probe):
axesTest.how_probe_text: the BLTouch measures the bed where the head is (G30 S-1, without changing Z). Then Z goes back and forth several times at the test speed and acceleration, and the probe measures again at the same place. If Z lost steps (both its motors together), the height does not match (more than {mm} mm). Leave the head over a clear bed before starting. The test limits are removed at the end.
axesTest.how_switch_text: the machine gently touches the endstop of the axis and notes where it thinks it is (without homing again). Then it goes back and forth several times at the test speed and acceleration, and touches the endstop again. If the motor lost steps, the second measurement does not match the first (more than {mm} mm of difference). The test limits are removed at the end.
axesTest.previous_test_interrupted: A previous test was interrupted: axis {axis} may still have test limits set.
axesTest.travel_too_short: With {mm} mm of travel some steps do not reach the requested speed (they need {need} mm).
axesTest.lost_steps_at: {axis} lost steps at {v} mm/min and {a} mm/s² (difference {d} mm).
axesTest.last_that_passed: Last one that passed: {v} mm/min, {a} mm/s². For working use ~80% of that.
axesTest.no_lost_steps_up_to: {axis}: no lost steps up to {v} mm/min and {a} mm/s².

startup.title: Start-up
startup.state_na: does not apply to your machine
startup.make_tip: Copies the example to the SD card. It never overwrites a file that already exists.
startup.edit_tip: Opens the file in the DWC editor.
startup.hide_tip: Hides this row on this screen. It does not delete anything.
startup.service_tip: It has to be running: it makes the examples and answers the buttons of this plugin.
startup.row_drivers_tip: The service reads the Duet drivers (M122, M569) while this screen is open. With no drivers in config.g there is nothing to show.
startup.drivers_none: the Duet declares no driver (check M584 and M569 in config.g)
startup.drivers_no_data: the service delivers no driver data
startup.row_macros_tip: The axis tests use macros of the plugin itself in 0:/sys/workshop/macros. They travel with it; if they are missing, reinstall it.
startup.assist_tip: Walks you through what is missing, one thing at a time. You can skip what you do not need.
startup.assist_no_action: This cannot be fixed with a file from here. Read the explanation and, when you have it, tap "Check again".
startup.assist_done_ready: Everything you went through is ready.
startup.assist_done_left: {n} left to do. You can start again whenever you like.
startup.create_help_tip: Asks a few questions and builds the file. Nothing is saved until you confirm.
startup.questions_intro: Answer and I will build the file. Nothing is saved until you confirm.
startup.err_range: The number is outside the allowed range.
startup.err_chars: Do not use quotes, semicolons or line breaks.
startup.err_pattern: It does not have the expected format. See the help of this field.
startup.warn_moves: {n} line(s) that move the machine were commented out with ";". Check them and remove the ";" only when you are sure and the machine is free.
startup.warn_active: Lines without ";" really run when you use the button.
startup.plan_example: {file} only has the example (all commented). It is replaced by this one, and the previous text is kept in {backup}.
startup.plan_new: {file} already has your configuration and I will not overwrite it. This one will be saved apart as {target}; when you have checked it, rename it in Files > Macros.
startup.verify_ok: Done: the file exists, has active instructions and the plugin already sees it.
startup.verify_new: Saved as {file}. The plugin keeps using the previous file until you swap the names.
startup.verify_comments: {file} was saved, but all its lines are still commented, so the plugin still takes it as an example. That may be what you wanted.
startup.verify_notseen: {file} was saved, but the plugin does not see it as ready yet. Tap "Check again" in a few seconds.
startup.verify_missing: I could not read {file} back. Tap "Check again" to verify it.
startup.verify_fail: It could not be saved ({error}). Nothing was changed.
startup.plan_changed: The file changed while you were answering. Check again what is going to happen and confirm once more.
startup.modal_hint: Tap a card to set it up, or let it walk you through step by step.
startup.modal_sub: Get ready what this plugin needs from your machine
startup.row_drivers_what: The drivers (controllers) of the motors that you declared in your config.g.
startup.row_drivers_for: The service reads them to show the current, temperature and faults of each motor.
startup.row_drivers_missing: The page stays empty. Check that your config.g declares the drivers and that the service is running.
startup.row_macros_what: Macros of the plugin itself for the axis tests.
startup.row_macros_missing: The tests do not work. Reinstall the plugin: the macros come with it.

faults.otpw_hint: The driver is hot (about 120 °C). Check the board ventilation and the current (M906).
faults.ot_hint: The driver shut down from heat (about 150 °C) and the motor lost its force. Let it cool, check the ventilation and the current, and home before going on.
faults.s2ga_hint: Short in the cable or the motor. Turn the power supply off and check the cable and connector of phase A.
faults.s2gb_hint: Short in the cable or the motor. Turn the power supply off and check the cable and connector of phase B.
faults.s2vsa_hint: Short between phase A and the supply. Turn the power supply off and check the motor wiring.
faults.s2vsb_hint: Short between phase B and the supply. Turn the power supply off and check the motor wiring.
faults.ola_hint: Only measured with the motor moving: check the connector and the cable of phase A (loose or cut).
faults.olb_hint: Only measured with the motor moving: check the connector and the cable of phase B (loose or cut).
faults.ext_hint: The external driver reports a fault: look at its indicator and its power.
faults.pos_tol_hint: Closed loop: the motor lags behind what was asked. Lower the acceleration or check the mechanics.
faults.pos_lost_hint: Closed loop: it lost its position. Home and check the tuning of the loop.
faults.setting_error_hint: Repeat the closed loop tuning of that driver.
faults.mov_ilegal: Move without the closed loop tuned
faults.mov_ilegal_hint: Tune the closed loop before moving.
faults.gstat_hint: A fault happened at some point (heat or a short) even if it is gone now. See the alerts of the period in Charts.

page.lead: How the motors are doing: state, charts, release, advisor, tests and crash detection.
page.enable_enabled_hint: The driver has current: the motor holds its position.
page.enable_released_hint: It moves by hand and lost its position. To go back: enable it and home.
page.enable_partial_hint: A driver of this axis is off: the axis can rack. Enable it and home.
page.enable_unknown_hint: CAN board or a driver that cannot be read: it is not known whether it is holding.
page.enable_unpowered_hint: The motor power supply is off: no motor is holding.
page.speed_hint: Cruise speed of the current move (RRF does not publish the instantaneous speed of each axis): on a diagonal each axis goes somewhat slower.
page.current_hint: Estimated from the driver's CS_ACTUAL (read every 5 s while this page is open): at rest it drops to the idle current.
page.waiting_report: Waiting for the motors report of the service...
page.no_motors: The machine has no axes or extruders with a motor.
page.stale_note: The data are not updating: what you see may not be current.
page.move_line: Current move: requested {req} mm/s, cruise {top} mm/s
page.move_limited: held back by the limits (M203 / M201 / M566)
page.banner_text: They move by hand and lost their position; a vertical axis can fall. To end it: enable them and home.
page.banner_power_off: With the power supply off they cannot be enabled.
page.enable_off_hint: The firmware has not energized it yet (after the board started) or it is not used: it gets its force with the first move or the homing.

details.hiccups_none: No reading: power supply off or no M122 data yet
details.hiccups_bad: The board was late with some steps and held the move back: lower the speed or the microstepping
details.hiccups_ok: 0: the board generates every step on time
details.board_rate: Steps per second of the board now
details.ceiling_measured: Ceiling measured on your board: {khz} kHz ({pct} %)
details.ceiling_none: No reference: measure the ceiling in Measure
details.kin_note_cartesian: Each motor is independent: a straight cut works a single axis.
details.kin_note_coreXY: Coupled: any move in X or Y moves both motors at once.
details.kin_note_coreXZ: Coupled like CoreXY, between X and Z.
details.kin_note_linearDelta: Coupled: any move moves the three towers at once.
details.kin_note_rotaryDelta: Coupled like the linear delta: three motors move together.
details.kin_note_other: A kinematics this plugin does not know: take the measured ceiling as the one of the whole board, not per motor.
details.rpm_note: with motors of {n} steps per revolution (change it in Advisor > Your motors data)
details.gstat_reset_hint: The driver restarted at some point (for example when the power supply was switched on). It is not a fault.
details.help_hiccups: the firmware counts them in M122: the times the step generator was late and had to hold the move back for an instant. 0 is what is expected; if they appear at some speed, the board cannot do more (lower the speed or the microstepping). To know whether a motor loses steps for lack of force use the Test section.
details.help_reference: if you measured the ceiling in the Measure section, it is the one of your board and your firmware. Otherwise dc42's table (Duet 3 6HC, RRF 3.2) for one motor is used, by the timing of the drivers.
details.help_speed: RRF does not publish the instantaneous speed of each axis: the cruise speed of the move being run is used, only for the axes that move (the still ones stay at 0). On a diagonal it is somewhat higher than the real one of each axis.
details.help_alerts: if the chip of the main board is known its DRV_STATUS register is read with M569.2 (read only), which also gives the current the driver applies. Otherwise, and on CAN boards, the state the firmware publishes is used (no current). An open coil is only measured while moving. With this page closed the drivers are not read.

sequence.endstop: sensorless end stop calibration of axis {axis}
